data: This course is a continuation of the course Mathematical Methods for Economics I, pitched at a more advanced level, particularly for students in year 4 (under FYUP). The students will be introduced to the mathematical tools and concepts that are most frequently used in economic models of the firm and consumer behavior. To this end, the course will cover the topics of optimization (both constrained and unconstrained) with one and more than one choice variable, linear programming models, differential equation, difference equations and integration. The course will also cover in more detail some of the topics learned in Mathematical Methods for Economics I, like matrix algebra, rules of differentiation and limit theorems with specific focus on economic applications. Throughout the course, we will take an intensive approach to mathematics, but most of the emphasis will be on the applications or economic models rather than abstract mathematical theorems or concepts.
